title.en: Lebanese army says troops deploying in 'pilot zone' after Israeli withdrawal
title.zh: 黎巴嫩军队称以色列撤军后部队将部署在“试点区”

summary.en: The Lebanese army announced the deployment of its troops in a "pilot zone" following the withdrawal of Israeli forces. This move is part of a US-brokered agreement for Israeli troops to pull out of a small area of Lebanon previously occupied during their conflict with Hezbollah.
summary.zh: 黎巴嫩军队宣布，在以色列撤军后，其部队将部署在一个“试点区”。此举是美国斡旋协议的一部分，该协议旨在让以色列军队撤出其在与真主党冲突期间占领的黎巴嫩一小部分地区。

body.en:
Lebanon's army says its troops are deploying to a "pilot zone" in the south of the country following the withdrawal of Israeli forces under a US-brokered agreement reached last month.

Engineering units entered the village of Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh in Nabatieh district on Tuesday morning, the army command announced.

Later, it said Israeli forces had opened fire in the vicinity of the troops. Israel's military said warning shots had been fired after the troops crossed into the Israeli-declared "security zone".

The pilot zone plan should see Israeli troops pulling out of a small part of the territory occupied during their conflict with Hezbollah and the disarmament of the Iran-backed Lebanese group.

Tuesday's deployment began ahead of a meeting in Washington between US President Donald Trump and his Lebanese counterpart, Joseph Aoun.

Aoun was expected to urge Trump to put pressure on Israel to withdraw from the rest of southern Lebanon and support the Lebanese army in taking full control of areas where Hezbollah holds sway.

"I told him [Trump] I need two things from you: political support and supporting the LAF [Lebanese Armed Forces]," Aoun told reporters in the Oval Office.

Speaking alongside Aoun, Trump vowed that the US would provide help to Lebanon which had been "hit hard" for decades.

"It's been a very badly treated place and country, and we're going to have it properly treated," he said. "And treated with the respect it deserves."

The US state department announced on Monday afternoon that "pilot zone operations" had begun in Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh and two other Lebanese villages, Froun and Srifa, in line with the Trilateral Framework agreed by Israel, Lebanon and the US at the end of June.

It said the "milestone" was the direct result of discussions last week between Israeli and Lebanese representatives in Rome.

Later on Monday, an Israeli military official confirmed the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) would "adjust its force posture in one of the pilot areas" to allow the Lebanese army to carry out its mission, while also "safeguarding the security of IDF soldiers and preserving its right to self-defence and to remove threats".

"The objective of the pilot and the agreement is the disarmament of the Hezbollah terrorist organisation and the removal of its illegal weapons," the official said.

They also reiterated that the IDF would remain in the "security zone" - the 10km (six-mile) deep strip of occupied Lebanese territory running along the border - for "as long as necessary" to defend northern Israeli communities.

body.zh: 黎巴嫩军队表示，在以色列军队根据上个月达成的美国斡旋协议撤军后，黎巴嫩军队正在部署到该国南部的“试验区”。 陆军司令部宣布，工兵部队于周二上午进入纳巴蒂耶区的扎塔尔加尔比耶村。 随后，又有消息称，以色列军队在部队附近开枪。以色列军方表示，部队进入以色列宣布的“安全区”后，已鸣枪警告。 试验区计划应该让以色列军队撤出在与真主党冲突期间占领的一小部分领土，并解除伊朗支持的黎巴嫩组织的武装。 周二的部署是在美国总统唐纳德·特朗普和黎巴嫩总统约瑟夫·奥恩在华盛顿举行会议之前开始的。 预计奥恩将敦促特朗普向以色列施压，要求其从黎巴嫩南部其他地区撤军，并支持黎巴嫩军队完全控制真主党控制的地区。 “我告诉他（特朗普），我需要你做两件事：政治支持和支持 LAF（黎巴嫩武装部队），”奥恩在椭圆形办公室对记者说。 特朗普与奥恩一起发表讲话，誓言美国将向几十年来遭受“沉重打击”的黎巴嫩提供帮助。 “这是一个受到非常恶劣对待的地方和国家，我们将妥善对待它，”他说。 “并受到应有的尊重。” 美国国务院周一下午宣布，根据以色列、黎巴嫩和美国 6 月底达成的三边框架，“试验区行动”已在 Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh 和另外两个黎巴嫩村庄 Froun 和 Srifa 开始。 声明称，这一“里程碑”是以色列和黎巴嫩代表上周在罗马讨论的直接结果。 周一晚些时候，一名以色列军方官员证实，以色列国防军将“调整其在一个试点地区的兵力态势”，以允许黎巴嫩军队执行任务，同时“保障以色列国防军士兵的安全，维护其自卫和消除威胁的权利”。 这位官员表示：“试点项目和协议的目标是解除真主党恐怖组织的武装并清除其非法武器。” 他们还重申，以色列国防军将在“必要时”留在“安全区”——沿边界延伸的10公里（六英里）深的黎巴嫩被占领土地带——以保卫以色列北部社区。 周二，黎巴嫩军队指挥部表示，“根据与黎巴嫩军事协调小组的持续沟通”，其部队已开始部署到 Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh，指的是成立的三边机构......

reflection.en: The withdrawal of troops following a brokered agreement highlights the difficult but vital work of peacemaking. Yahweh blesses those who actively seek to bridge divides and bring an end to conflict, even in small, contested areas. Such steps, however modest, are crucial for fostering stability and hope.
reflection.zh: 军队根据协议撤出，彰显了缔造和平这项艰巨而重要的工作。雅伟赐福那些积极寻求弥合分歧、结束冲突的人，即使是在小范围的争议地区。这些步骤，无论多么微小，对于促进稳定和希望都至关重要。

verse.textEn: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.

title.en: Fiscal hawk or big spender – what kind of chancellor will John Healey be?

Kennedy made the remarks one day after the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) did an about-face on a 27-state recall of shredded iceberg lettuce, calling the reported product a “false positive”. title.en: Carney looking at 'all options' as Trump announces 50% tariffs on Canada
title.zh: 特朗普宣布对加拿大征收 50% 关税，卡尼正在考虑“所有选择”

summary.en: The duties mark a major escalation in trade tensions between the North American neighbours.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump has imposed a 50% tariff on a wide range of goods imported from Canada, in retaliation for what he called "unequal treatment" of US cars, dairy and alcohol.

Everyday consumer items like wine and hockey sticks, as well as industrial goods such as cement, are on the target list. Several key exports, though, will be spared, including energy, potash, critical minerals and fish.

Prime Minister Mark Carney said he had spoken to Trump and both leaders agreed to "intensify" trade talks in a bid to calm growing trade tensions between the North American neighbours.

But he warned "all options" were on the table in terms of how Canada could respond to the fresh tariff threat.

Since the tariff war broke out more than 18 months ago, Carney said, Canadians have "stood together" by buying home-produced goods and agreeing new trade routes with other countries.

"[The] country is stronger, stronger because we are united, and we will remain united," he told reporters.

Tensions between the major trading partners have been simmering since Trump returned to office in January last year and unleashed a wide-ranging global programme of tariffs, sometimes to pursue objectives not directly linked to trade.

Tariffs are taxes on imported goods that are paid to the government by companies bringing in the foreign products.

Asked about the latest tariffs, which the White House says will take effect in 30 days, on Tuesday, President Trump said Canada had been "very, very tough on us over the years" and "no other presidents done anything about it".

"I love Canada, I love the people of Canada, many friends that live in Canada," he said. "Without us, there's no way they can survive."

The latest move by Trump comes after the US Supreme Court ruled earlier this year that many of the tariffs imposed globally under emergency powers were illegally enacted. The president has since sought other legal avenues to push through his flagship trade policy , as seen in Monday's announcement.

Trump has said the levies will boost American manufacturing and jobs, but some economists have warned that higher charges on imported goods risks pushing up prices for consumers.

This new round of duties on Canadian goods has also fuelled speculation about a potential wider tariff announcement by the US on countries across the world. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said on Tuesday that he expected to "see some action soon", when asked on CNBC about the possibility of forthcoming levies.

Canada, which is one of the US's closest trading partners, was one of the few countries to retaliate last year against Trump's tariffs, placing a 25% levy of its own on about C$30bn (£16bn; $21.7bn) worth of US goods.

title.en: Two French firefighters die tackling blaze near Bordeaux airport
title.zh: 两名法国消防员在波尔多机场附近扑灭大火时丧生

summary.en: The blaze close to the parking lots at Bordeaux-Mérignac Airport is said to have originated from a brush fire.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Two firefighters have died while battling a huge blaze near Bordeaux's airport in south-west France, officials have said.

Reports in French media say the blaze, near one of the parking lots at the airport, originated from a brush fire and then spread to a building.

Pictures shared on social media show passengers getting off a plane as a massive plume of smoke rises nearby. A number of flights scheduled to arrive at Bordeaux–Mérignac airport have been delayed.

Some 100 firefighters, backed by specialist aircraft, are reported to be trying to extinguish the blaze.

The country's Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said he had been informed about the deaths by officials in the Gironde department.

Speaking during Tuesday's question-and-answer session at the French parliament, Nuñez also said he would travel to Gironde "as soon as possible" to oversee the firefighting efforts.

Gironde is one of several French departments ravaged by wildfires in recent days, due to a series of unusual and prolonged heatwaves.

The blaze in the Pontevès commune "is currently out of control and is evolving rapidly", said the PSFDF volunteer association, which monitors fires across France.

It said 500 firefighters and rescuers had been deployed to contain the fire, and 150 people had already been evacuated.

France has registered nearly 11,000 fires since the beginning of the year, with President Emmanuel Macron saying last week that there had not been so many blazes in the country since World War Two.

Tuesday's satellite data from the European Forest Fire Information System (Effis) shows that more than 42,000 hectares (103,784 acres) burned in France between January and mid-July, surpassing the previous record set in 2022.

Climate change is driving up temperatures around the world, and Europe is the fastest warming continent, heating up twice as fast as the global average, according to the Copernicus Climate Change Service.

This is causing increased summer heatwaves, greater pressure on Europe's water supply, and more intense wildfires.

The record-breaking temperatures across Europe this summer have led to major wildfires, most notably in Spain where at least 13 people have been killed.

Some 29,000 hectares of land have been destroyed by a massive wildfire north of the Spanish capital Madrid.
body.zh: 官员称，两名消防员在法国西南部波尔多机场附近扑灭大火时丧生。 法国媒体报道称，机场一个停车场附近的大火源于灌木丛火灾，然后蔓延到一栋建筑物。 社交媒体上分享的照片显示，乘客们正在下飞机，附近升起大量烟雾。一些原定抵达波尔多梅里尼亚克机场的航班已被延误。 据报道，大约 100 名消防员在特种飞机的支援下正在努力扑灭大火。 该国内政部长洛朗·努涅斯表示，吉伦特省官员已向他通报了死亡事件。 努涅斯在周二法国议会的问答会上发表讲话时还表示，他将“尽快”前往吉伦特省监督消防工作。 由于一系列不寻常且持续的热浪，吉伦特省是最近几天遭受野火袭击的法国几个省之一。 负责监测法国各地火灾情况的 PSFDF 志愿者协会表示，庞特韦斯公社的大火“目前已经失控，并且正在迅速蔓延”。 据称，已部署 500 名消防员和救援人员来控制火势，并已疏散 150 人。 自今年年初以来，法国已发生近 11,000 起火灾，法国总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙 (Emmanuel Macron) 上周表示，自第二次世界大战以来，法国从未发生过如此多的火灾。 欧洲森林火灾信息系统 (Effis) 周二的卫星数据显示，1 月至 7 月中旬，法国燃烧面积超过 42,000 公顷（103,784 英亩），超过了 2022 年创下的纪录。 根据哥白尼气候变化服务中心的数据，气候变化正在推高世界各地的气温，而欧洲是变暖最快的大陆，升温速度是全球平均水平的两倍。 这导致夏季热浪加剧、欧洲供水压力更大以及野火更加猛烈。 今年夏天，欧洲各地破纪录的气温导致了严重的山火，尤其是西班牙，造成至少 13 人死亡。 西班牙首都马德里北部的一场大规模野火摧毁了约 29,000 公顷土地。

title.zh: 美国对伊朗发动新一轮袭击，特朗普警告将对士兵死亡进行报复

summary.en: The United States has launched new strikes against Iran, following a warning from former President Trump about retaliation for the deaths of soldiers. Iran, in turn, claims to have targeted two ships in the Strait of Hormuz and sites in Bahrain and Jordan.

body.en:
The US military says it launched another round of strikes against Iran to "further degrade" its capabilities to attack ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

The 10th consecutive night of strikes took place after US President Donald Trump vowed to punish Iran for the deaths of US soldiers.

In response, Iran said it struck two oil tankers in the waterway, as well as US military assets in Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan, state news agency IRNA reported.

President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran was now fighting a "full-scale war" with the US. Trump earlier said Iran had been hit "very hard" the previous night "in honour" of three US soldiers killed recently - two in Jordan and one in Iraq.

US Central Command (Centcom) said its latest strikes had hit Iranian "military command centres, maritime capabilities, missile and drone launch sites, and air defence systems".

Explosions were reported near the north-western city of Tabriz, where state media said one person was killed and several wounded, as well at the Gulf ports of Bandar Mahshahr and Bandar Imam Khomeini and the south-eastern ports of Chabahar and Konarak.

Centcom also insisted that commercial vessels were continuing to pass through the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran meanwhile said its forces struck two oil tankers as they attempted to transit through what it called the strait's "unsafe and hazardous southern route" and rescue teams were picking up their crews, according to state media.

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) said a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz had reported being struck by an unknown projectile, forcing its crew to abandon the vessel and board a lifeboat.

It was not clear whether the tanker reported by UKMTO was among those cited by Iran.

Six fuel tankers and cargo ships crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, according to preliminary data from maritime intelligence firm Kpler. Two of these vessels had previously been sanctioned by the US for links with Iran.

This is down from eight vessels crossing on 19 July, the data shows. All but one of the crossings made on 20 July were via the northern route near Iran.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) also claimed to have targeted a data centre belonging to the US company Amazon in Bahrain, according to state media on Tuesday.

The IRGC "attacked and destroyed the central data infrastructure of the American company Amazon in Bahrain with several cruise missiles," state news agency IRNA reported.

Jordan said on Tuesday that it had intercepted five drones after saying it had shot down three missiles late on Monday. Bahrain said drones launched by Iran had targeted its air navigation systems - but traffic remained unaffected. Kuwait's armed forces also said they had intercepted Iranian drones.

title.en: Brazil's Amazon sees sharp decline in size of area burned in 2025
title.zh: 巴西亚马逊地区2025年烧毁面积大幅下降

summary.en: The amount of land burned in the world's largest rainforest was the smallest since MapBiomas records began in 1985, marking a significant decline in deforestation and fires.
summary.zh: 亚马逊雨林被烧毁的面积创下MapBiomas自1985年有记录以来的最低点，标志着森林砍伐和火灾的显著减少。

body.en:
The area burned in Brazil's Amazon in 2025 was far smaller in size than the previous year, according to the deforestation monitoring group MapBiomas.

A MapBiomas report states that 3.1 million hectares of Brazil's Amazon were burned last year, compared with a record-breaking 15.8 million hectares in 2024.

The amount of land burned in the world's largest rainforest last year covered the smallest area since MapBiomas records began in 1985.

Protecting the Amazon was one of the pledges President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva made when he was running for running for office four years ago. These latest figures will be seen as a boost to his campaign for re-election in October.

In 2024, the Amazon rainforest experienced its worst forest fires in over two decades, which the Copernicus Climate Change Service put down to "climate extremes and human activity".

"The 2025 figures are significant and show that it is possible to reduce the burned area in the country," Vera Arruda, a researcher at the Amazon Environmental Research Institute (IPAM) and co-ordinator at MapBiomas, told the BBC.

"The 31% drop compared to the historical average - driven primarily by the lowest number of fires recorded in the Amazon in 41 years - is positive news, but it does not yet allow us to conclude that this is an established trend or to scale back prevention efforts," Arruda added.

The MapBiomas report shows a dramatic drop in area burned not just in the Amazon, but across the whole of Brazil in 2025.

Figures show around 12.7 million hectares burned in Brazil in 2025, compared to 30 million hectares in 2024.

The highest number of hectares burned in Brazil since records began was in 2007, when 30.7 million were recorded across the country.

The decline in the 2025 figures partly reflects an easing of the unprecedented fires of 2024, helped by cooler La Niña conditions instead of the warmer El Niño.

But MapBiomas warned the natural weather pattern of El Niño, which pushes up global temperatures, could extend this year's dry season and increase the risk of forest fires.

Tropical rainforests like the Amazon are home to millions of species, and in a healthy state they absorb vast quantities of planet-warming carbon dioxide, helping to keep the Earth cool.

They have come under increasing pressure as a result of decades of deliberate land clearance for agriculture and logging, as well as climate change, which scientists warn can create the conditions for bigger fires to spread.

When he took office, President Lula promised to reverse the deforestation which occurred during the presidency of his predecessor, Jair Bolsonaro.

title.en: China narrows AI gap, challenges US influence
title.zh: 中国缩小人工智能差距，挑战美国影响力

summary.en: At the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai, Beijing showcased advances in AI while promoting its vision of open-source development and global governance.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
At the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai, Beijing showcased advances in AI while promoting its vision of open-source development and global governance.

As China narrows the artificial intelligence (AI) gap with the United States,  Beijing is promoting a narrative centered on "open source" and "inclusive AI" as an argument for its vision of global governance.

During his keynote speech at the World Artificial Intelligence Conference (WAIC) in Shanghai on Friday, Chinese President Xi Jinping expressed China's ambition to take a leading role in setting global standards in AI . He criticized what he described as the "overextension of the concept of national security."

Xi did not openly reference the United States. However, Beijing's effort to position itself as an advocate of a new AI order and challenge US dominance was unmistakable.

This year's Shanghai summit sent several important signals, says Rogier Creemers, assistant professor at Leiden University in the Netherlands specializing in China's digital technology policy. The WAIC indicates that artificial intelligence is now one of Beijing's political priorities, and that China intends to compete with the United States by supporting open-source AI models and promoting AI-driven industrialization, Creemers told DW. He also noted China hopes to win support from countries in the Global South for this effort.

China is steadily narrowing the gap with the United States in AI model development, and its efforts at AI application in industrial processes are slowly maturing. 

Chinese AI model developers have continued to keep pace on the global stage, largely by training open-weight models on limited but advanced computer hardware, Paul Triolo, senior vice president for China and tech policy lead at DGA-Albright Stonebridge Group, told DW.

Triolo believes deployment of AI across Chinese enterprises may be progressing faster than in the United States.

In addition, there is less fear of AI among the Chinese population than there is in the US, facilitating more rapid uptake of AI applications at the consumer level.

Earlier this year, Chinese state media claimed that the performance gap between Chinese and US AI models had "largely disappeared."

Several experts broadly agreed with this assessment, saying that certain benchmark tests of China's  large language models (LLMs) such as GLM-5.2 and Kimi K3 showed the gap narrowing or even fully closing.

For most applications, Triolo noted, China's leading open-weight AI models are cheaper to run and more than capable of handling most tasks.

body.zh: 在上海举行的世界人工智能大会上，北京展示了人工智能的进步，同时宣传其开源发展和全球治理的愿景。 随着中国缩小与美国的人工智能 (AI) 差距，北京正在推动以“开源”和“包容性人工智能”为中心的叙事，作为其全球治理愿景的论据。 中国国家主席习近平周五在上海举行的世界人工智能大会（WAIC）上发表主旨演讲时表达了中国在制定人工智能全球标准方面发挥主导作用的雄心。他批评他所说的“国家安全概念的过度延伸”。 习近平没有公开提及美国。 然而，北京将自己定位为人工智能新秩序倡导者并挑战美国主导地位的努力是明确无误的。 荷兰莱顿大学专门研究中国数字技术政策的助理教授罗吉尔·克里默斯表示，今年的上海峰会发出了几个重要信号。 Creemers 告诉德国之声，WAIC 表明人工智能现在是北京的政治优先事项之一，中国打算通过支持开源人工智能模型和促进人工智能驱动的工业化来与美国竞争。他还指出，中国希望为此赢得南方国家的支持。 中国在人工智能模型开发方面与美国的差距正在稳步缩小，人工智能在工业流程中的应用也正在慢慢成熟。 DGA-Albright Stonebridge Group 中国区高级副总裁兼技术政策负责人 Paul Triolo 告诉德国之声，中国人工智能模型开发人员继续在全球舞台上保持同步，主要是在有限但先进的计算机硬件上训练开放权重模型。 Triolo 认为，中国企业的人工智能部署进展可能比美国更快。 此外，中国民众对人工智能的恐惧程度低于美国民众，这有助于消费者更快速地接受人工智能应用。 今年早些时候，中国官方媒体声称中国和美国人工智能模型之间的性能差距已经“基本消失”。 多位专家普遍同意这一评估，并表示，GLM-5.2和Kimi K3等中国大型语言模型（LLM）的某些基准测试表明，差距正在缩小甚至完全缩小。 Triolo 指出，对于大多数应用程序来说，中国领先的开放式人工智能模型的运行成本更低，并且能够处理大多数任务。 与此同时，Anthropic、OpenAI 和 Google 等美国领先公司的先进专有模型仍然在以下领域保持优势……

reflection.en: This story draws attention to peace-making and restraint. Matthew 5:9 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with mercy, truth, and restraint, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.

title.en: How India's youth-led 'Cockroach' movement challenges Modi
title.zh: 印度青年主导的“蟑螂”运动如何挑战莫迪

summary.en: A satirical protest in India against exam leaks has evolved into a significant youth-led movement. This movement now expresses broader discontent among young Indians regarding employment opportunities and educational issues.
summary.zh: 印度一场针对考试泄题的讽刺性抗议活动，已演变为一场由青年主导的更广泛的运动。该运动表达了印度年轻人对就业和教育问题日益增长的不满。

body.en:
What started as a satirical protest against exam leaks in India has grown into a wider movement voicing young Indians' anger over jobs and education.

Riot police fired tear gas and used batons in New Delhi as tens of thousands of supporters of the satirical Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) marched towards India's Parliament on Monday (July 20).

Police in the Indian capital said 60 protesters and 118 police officers were injured in the clashes between demonstrators and security forces. Mobile internet was suspended in parts of the city, including around the Jantar Mantar protest site, during the violence.

Protesters are demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Earlier this year, authorities canceled the high-stakes NEET medical entrance exam over a leaked question paper , affecting millions of students and sparking outrage across India .

The CJP began as an online campaign in May and rapidly evolved into a Gen Z street movement , giving a voice to a generation frustrated by unemployment, shrinking opportunities and a failing education system.

The youth-led "Cockroach" party is now posing an unexpected challenge for Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government , prompting a response that combines political outreach with police action.

Modi's rivals have also tried to step in and take advantage of the youth's frustrations.

"Is this how a government behaves? Using tear gas and baton charges against students? This is a worthless government," Renuka Chowdhury, an MP from India's opposition Congress party, told DW.

The CJP movement  gained fresh momentum over the weekend after veteran reform activist Sonam Wangchuk, whose three-week hunger strike has become a symbol of the protests, was forcibly taken to a hospital by police . 

It is not the first time India has experienced major protest movements. Hunger strikes, famously used by Mahatma Gandhi, remain a common and peaceful form of protest in India.

India Against Corruption (IAC) led by veteran activist Anna Hazare, managed to mobilize millions in 2011 and reshape the country's political landscape. A decade later, yearlong farmers' protests forced Modi to repeal controversial farm laws. However, a 2023 Olympic wrestlers' protest over allegations of sexual harassment achieved few of their goals, despite widespread sympathy.

Analysts say the CJP lacks a nationwide organizational network, which the farmers had at their disposal. Yet like the IAC movement, it has tapped into a broader public mood.

reflection.en: When young people feel their future is at stake due to systemic issues, their collective voice can rise as a powerful call for change. Yahweh's word reminds us that true justice should flow consistently and powerfully, addressing the deep-seated concerns of a society.

title.en: The founder never intended it to get so big: How a 'cockroach' movement is taking hold
title.zh: 创始人从未想过它会变得如此之大：“蟑螂”运动如何扎根

summary.en: A student-led movement in India has grown into a broader campaign for accountability and restoration of trust in institutions.
summary.zh: 印度的一场学生运动已发展成为一场更广泛的运动，旨在呼吁问责制并重建人们对机构的信任。

body.en:
Thousands of protesters clashed with police in India on Monday as they tried to march to parliament to demand the education minister's resignation.

Police fired tear gas and charged at demonstrators with batons after they tried to breach security barricades surrounding the protest site in central New Delhi.

This marked one of the most serious confrontations in a youth-led movement's campaign against Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government.

The protesters describe themselves as the Cockroach Janta Party, a movement that erupted online two months ago and gained momentum over alleged leaks on social media in the country’s fiercely competitive college entrance exams.

Here's how India's youth embraced an insult as a badge of resilience and turned it into a satirical political campaign that amassed millions of followers.

The movement began in May after India's supreme court chief justice Surya Kant compared some unemployed young people to "cockroaches" and "parasites" during a hearing on another issue.

Abhijeet Dipke, a 30-year-old public relations graduate who was looking for work in the United States at the time, said he was "taken aback" by the comments made by Kant — who later said they were taken out of context.

Despite rapid economic growth, millions of people in the world's most populous nation struggle to find stable and well-paying jobs, fuelling discontent.

"How can the custodian of the constitution compare the youth with cockroaches and parasites, just for expressing their opinions and criticising the system?" Dipke told Agence France-Presse (AFP).

Dipke then went online in May to air his frustrations, making a satirical post on X that said: "What if all cockroaches come together?"

But the post went viral, driving Dipke to transform the idea into a parody platform that he named the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), playing on the name of the country's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

"Within two hours we got some 5,000 sign-ups on the Google form ... and that made me realise — why not launch an official website and a manifesto?" Dipke said.

More than 30,000 people joined within 24 hours of its launch. It now has more than 23 million followers on its Instagram account, eclipsing the BJP's by 14 million followers.

"That is when I realised maybe the youth here is trying to send a message," he said.

Dipke said momentum for the movement has been largely driven by gen Z students in their 20s.

"They told me they are really dissatisfied with all the existing political parties, because nobody listens to them," he said.

title.en: Netanyahu may visit New York. Mamdani and Trump disagree on what awaits him
title.zh: 内塔尼亚胡可能访问纽约。马姆达尼和特朗普就他将面临的局面意见不一

summary.en: Israel has dismissed an international court's arrest warrant for its prime minister as 'bogus', amidst reports of a potential visit to New York and differing opinions from commentators on the implications.
summary.zh: 以色列驳斥了国际法院对其总理发出的逮捕令为“虚假”的说法，此前有报道称总理可能访问纽约，且评论员对此可能面临的局面意见不一。

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump has reassured Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that he will not face arrest in the US, after New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani said he was considering options for such a move.

The International Criminal Court (ICC) issued arrest warrants for Netanyahu in 2024, accusing him of using starvation as a method of warfare and intentionally directing attacks against civilians in Gaza. Israel has denied allegations of war crimes.

Mamdani told the New York Times newspaper that his city's legal department was actively considering legal options for Netanyahu's arrest, should the Israeli leader come to New York for the UN General Assembly in September.

"I believe that Prime Minister Netanyahu belongs in The Hague. He's a war criminal who has been charged by the International Criminal Court," he said.

"I've also said that I will follow the laws that we have here in New York City because I believe that there is an importance in following the law as a leader who presides over our city."

He said he would use existing laws, not create new ones, to potentially enforce the ICC warrant.

"Whatever the law allows me to do in New York City, that's what we will do, but we won't be writing our own laws to that end."

On Tuesday, Trump said the Israeli prime minister would not be arrested in the US, while not addressing Mamdani's comments directly.

"Benjamin Netanyahu will not be arrested, in any way, shape, or form, while in the United States of America," he said in a post on his Truth Social platform, adding that Netanyahu was assisting in the US' war against Iran.

"The only ones that should be arrested are the people that led Iran into this unprecedented SPIRAL OF DEATH AND DESTRUCTION."

Netanyahu's office earlier responded to Mamdani's comments, describing the warrant as "bogus" and the actions of the ICC prosecutor Karim Khan as "criminal". Khan is facing sexual misconduct allegations that he denies .

"The ICC is a kangaroo court that has no jurisdiction over Americans or Israelis," the office posted.

"Mamdani appears interested in diverting public attention from his follies and attacking the leader of the Jewish state and the only democracy in the Middle East."

title.en: 'Kings of the World': Spain's World Cup stars get a hero's welcome from fans and royals
title.zh: “世界之王”：西班牙世界杯球星受到球迷和王室的英雄式欢迎

summary.en: Spain's World Cup-winning football team received a hero's welcome from the country's royals and celebrated with a bus parade through Madrid.

body.en:
New World Cup champions Spain enjoyed a vibrant celebration parade on an open-top bus through the streets of Madrid on Monday evening, with a jubilant crowd of an estimated two million people out to celebrate, according to local authorities.

The players, some shirtless, others holding drinks, set off on their procession under a blazing sun, along the main arteries in the city centre where a sea of fans in red and yellow were waiting, before arriving at Cibeles square where they took to the stage and partied into the night.

The squad and coach Luis de la Fuente were introduced one by one to the fans, each with their own choice of music that they sung along to, wearing "We are champions" shirts.

"(Spain) showed the world what it is to work together, with one mind and one heart," said pop superstar Shakira in a video message played to the team and crowd.

De la Fuente offered a similar message, hailing his players as the "best in the world" and telling fans not to forget that "together we are stronger".

After flying back from the United States to Madrid, the players were received by King Felipe VI and the royal family earlier Monday, and then Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez Pérez-Castejón, before kicking off the parade.

Players passed around the gleaming World Cup trophy and waved to their adoring supporters, some lining balconies, others on top of bus stops, the day after defeating Argentina 1-0 in extra-time in New Jersey.

Ferran Torres's strike in extra-time was enough to bring Spain their second World Cup, following a first victory in 2010.

"You have shown your grit, your resilience and your courage ... combining head and heart," the king told La Roja's stars, who were dressed in suits but changed to more casual clothing for their parade on a hot summer's day.

"Kings of the world" ran the words on the front of their vehicle, with fans chanting "champions" to their heroes.

Spain captain Rodri held the World Cup trophy aloft at the top of the stairs as he descended from the Iberia plane that flew the team home after clinching their second star.

Later at Moncloa, Manchester City midfielder Rodri said this was the crowning achievement of his career.

"I've always said it, winning with your country is the most beautiful thing there is, above all a World Cup," said Rodri.

"This generation grew up watching (Iker) Casillas and (Andres) Iniesta lift the cup and that we can do it today is the biggest thing you can do in football."

Many younger supporters were not yet born when Iniesta's extra-time goal against the Netherlands secured Spain's first World Cup in South Africa 16 years ago.

title.en: Yemen's Houthis declare Saudi maritime blockade, threatening new front in US-Iran war

body.en:
Yemen's Houthi rebels announced a maritime embargo of Saudi Arabia overnight, stepping up the US-Iran war as the rebels threatened the top oil exporter's ability to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.

The Iran-backed group did not say how it planned to impose the embargo, whose declaration came as Iran said it was back to a "full-scale war" with the United States, and as Washington and Tehran battled to control the strait .

Saudi Arabia and the Houthis traded fire last week for the first time in years, threatening a 2022 truce that has held despite expiring .

The exchange of strikes was set off when an Iranian plane attempted to land in Sanaa, challenging Saudi Arabia's hegemony over Yemeni skies.

The Houthis' naval blockade, if enforced, could further strain Saudi Arabia's economy by cutting off access to its Red Sea ports, which have been vital for oil exports as renewed fighting limits passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

The blockade is also expected to hurt global markets that rely on Saudi Arabia — which produces over 10 million barrels of crude per day — for energy imports.

The rebels declared "a maritime embargo against the criminal Saudi enemy, based on the equation of 'an eye for an eye', effective immediately", military spokesman Yahya Saree said.

Stephane Dujarric, spokesman for the UN secretary-general, warned that the threat from the Houthis risked an "even wider" regional conflict.

The Houthis have previously tried to cut off shipping through the Red Sea, leveraging the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a chokepoint at its southern tip which vessels must navigate when travelling to or from the Suez Canal and the Mediterranean.

Security expert Andreas Krieg said Tehran could ask the Houthis to "prepare the Bab al-Mandab front and may provide the strategic trigger, particularly if US pressure is degrading Iran's position around Hormuz" even if the rebels retain "considerable autonomy".

The full closure of the Bab al-Mandab strait would reduce global oil supply by 7 per cent as it would leave most of Saudi oil exports unable to leave the region. The disruption would add to the huge cut to oil flows from the US-Iran war, which has already reduced shipments by 10 per cent of global supply.

"A simultaneous crisis at Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab would produce a much larger shock than either blockade alone," the King's College London academic told Agence France-Presse.

"Hormuz disruption constrains Gulf oil and liquefied natural gas exports, while Bab al-Mandab disruption interrupts the principal maritime connection between Asia, the Gulf and Europe."

summary.en: Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada, a co-founder of the notorious Sinaloa cartel and one of the world's most wanted drug traffickers, has been sentenced to life without parole in a US prison.

body.en:
Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada, a co-founder of the Sinaloa cartel and one of the world's most notorious drug traffickers, was sentenced to life in a US prison.

Mexican drug trafficker Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole on Tuesday for co-founding and leading the notorious Sinaloa cartel .

Zambada was one of the most prominent Mexican drug traffickers to face sentencing in a United States court since Joaquin "El Chapo" Guzman was sentenced to life in prison in 2019.

"The almost unimaginable amount of drugs attributable to him and the number of murders that we can document is enough to justify Congress's decision to make this a mandatory life sentence," US District Judge Brian Cogan said.

The 76-year-old Zambada apologized "for the harm I caused and for the example I set," urging future generations to "choose a different path."

He was arrested in July 2024 after he said he was kidnapped in Mexico and flown to Texas .

Zambada helped found and lead the Sinaloa cartel, becoming one of the most wanted figures for US intelligence and law enforcement agencies for decades.

According to prosecutors, he ordered torture and plotted murders, including the killing of his own nephew, as the cartel flooded the US with tons of cocaine, fentanyl, methamphetamine and other drugs .

He pleaded guilty to charges that included engaging in a continuing criminal enterprise and racketeering conspiracy, acknowledging culpability for 85 underlying crimes. In exchange, prosecutors did not seek the death penalty.

"I grew up in an environment where violence and crime seemed normal, but now I know that's no excuse," Zambada said in court on Monday. "There comes a time when every person must take responsibility for their decisions. I didn't, and many people paid the price."

Zambada's former partner "El Chapo" is already serving a life sentence in the United States.

He was convicted in 2019 and is serving a life sentence at the federal Supermax prison in Florence, Colorado.

Together they built the Sinaloa cartel into one of the world's most powerful drug trafficking organizations.

The Sinaloa cartel is one of six Mexican drug gangs that US President Donald Trump has designated as Foreign Terrorist Organizations.

Zambada was arrested with El Chapo's son, Joaquin Guzman Lopez , one of El Chapo's sons, who has pleaded guilty to federal drug charges. He has yet to be sentenced.

Zambada's arrest led to a splintering of the Sinaloa cartel, pitting his loyalists against backers of Guzman's sons, dubbed the Chapitos, or "little Chapos."

title.en: AliExpress hit with record EU fine
title.zh: 速卖通遭遇欧盟创纪录罚款

summary.en: The Chinese retailer has become the latest major online marketplace to face penalties under the EU’s Digital Services Act.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Chinese retailer has become the latest major online marketplace to face penalties under the EU’s Digital Services Act.

AliExpress said it plans to appeal a penalty imposed by European Union (EU) regulators, who found shortcomings in the firm's efforts to curb illegal, unsafe and counterfeit goods.

The largest Chinese e-commerce platform in the EU, AliExpress, has been fined  €550 million ($629 million) for failing to tackle sales of illegal, unsafe and counterfeit products.

"The spread of counterfeit clothing, unsafe toys, dangerous cosmetics and other illegal and harmful products is not an unavoidable cost of shopping online - it is a failure by AliExpress to comply with its obligations under the Digital Services Act," European Commission Vice President Henna Virkkunen said on Monday.

It is the largest fine ever imposed under the Digital Services Act (DSA) , which sets out clear rules for online services in the EU, targeting especially very large online platforms.

AliExpress said it will appeal the "disproportionate" fine, saying it considers the penalty excessive.

The online retail giant, which belongs to the Alibaba Group, must pay the fine and has until October 20, to submit a plan to address the breaches. EU regulators will then review the plan, after which the company could face further penalties.

A year ago, AliExpress agreed to tighten controls on illegal and potentially dangerous goods, such as medicines and supplements. But the European Commission said the measures did not fully resolve its broader concerns.

But AliExpress said the EU's decision "ignores our sound risk management framework and the significant, proactive enhancements we have made."

The company also said it has worked with the Commission to meet its "evolving expectations."

According to the EU, AliExpress has 193 million users in the bloc, ahead of online fashion giant Shein and retailer Temu, which have 156 million and 130 million users, respectively.

"One in five Europeans say they shop once a month from Shein, Temu and AliExpress," Virkkunen said.

Temu was fined  €200 million in May , while Elon Musk's social media platform X was fined in December last year, both for DSA violations.

body.en:
At the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai, Beijing showcased advances in AI while promoting its vision of open-source development and global governance.

As China narrows the artificial intelligence (AI) gap with the United States,  Beijing is promoting a narrative centered on "open source" and "inclusive AI" as an argument for its vision of global governance.

During his keynote speech at the World Artificial Intelligence Conference (WAIC) in Shanghai on Friday, Chinese President Xi Jinping expressed China's ambition to take a leading role in setting global standards in AI . He criticized what he described as the "overextension of the concept of national security."

Xi did not openly reference the United States. However, Beijing's effort to position itself as an advocate of a new AI order and challenge US dominance was unmistakable.

This year's Shanghai summit sent several important signals, says Rogier Creemers, assistant professor at Leiden University in the Netherlands specializing in China's digital technology policy. The WAIC indicates that artificial intelligence is now one of Beijing's political priorities, and that China intends to compete with the United States by supporting open-source AI models and promoting AI-driven industrialization, Creemers told DW. He also noted China hopes to win support from countries in the Global South for this effort.

China is steadily narrowing the gap with the United States in AI model development, and its efforts at AI application in industrial processes are slowly maturing. 

Chinese AI model developers have continued to keep pace on the global stage, largely by training open-weight models on limited but advanced computer hardware, Paul Triolo, senior vice president for China and tech policy lead at DGA-Albright Stonebridge Group, told DW.

Triolo believes deployment of AI across Chinese enterprises may be progressing faster than in the United States.

In addition, there is less fear of AI among the Chinese population than there is in the US, facilitating more rapid uptake of AI applications at the consumer level.

Earlier this year, Chinese state media claimed that the performance gap between Chinese and US AI models had "largely disappeared."

Several experts broadly agreed with this assessment, saying that certain benchmark tests of China's  large language models (LLMs) such as GLM-5.2 and Kimi K3 showed the gap narrowing or even fully closing.

For most applications, Triolo noted, China's leading open-weight AI models are cheaper to run and more than capable of handling most tasks.

summary.en: China and the Philippines traded accusations after a violent altercation between navy personnel in the disputed South China Sea. The incident heightened tensions ahead of a major diplomatic summit in Manila.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
China and the Philippines traded accusations after a violent altercation between navy personnel in the disputed South China Sea. The incident heightened tensions ahead of a major diplomatic summit in Manila.

Sailors from the Chinese and Philippine navies faced off with oars and batons in the disputed South China Sea , with Philippine officials saying that one of its sailors suffered a head injury as a result of the altercation.

The latest confrontation took place on Monday near the Second Thomas Shoal, a contested area where the two countries have repeatedly clashed before .  The  Philippines keeps a military presence in the area aboard the grounded warship BRP Sierra Madre.

Manila said that Chinese Coast Guard personnel had assaulted Filipino sailors as they approached the outpost. 

China quickly rejected this narrative. Beijing's Foreign Ministry said in a statement that the "Philippine side provoked the incident first," by approaching the Chinese vessel in small rubber boats, but then "turned around ​and made counter-accusations, distorted the facts and engaged in malicious ​hype."

On Tuesday, China summoned the Philippine ambassador in Beijing to lodge its complaints, with the Philippines quickly following suit with the Chinese counterpart in Manila.

The Second Thomas Shoal is part of the Spratly islands, a disputed archipelago in the South China Sea.

The Spratlys are key to Beijing's claim of the entire South China Sea, a key global trade route. Beijing maintains its claim to the waterway despite a 2016 ruling by the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague that there is no legal basis to its argument.

China has repeatedly demanded the removal of the outpost on the BRP Sierra Madre, and surrounded the atoll with its ships in a tense territorial standoff that has dragged on for years.

The incident came just ahead of a meeting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) which was set to begin on Tuesday with foreign ministers of the eleven member states and external partners.

Australia's Foreign Minister Penny Wong, who was in Manila for the summit, denounced Beijing on Tuesday for what she called "destabilizing and dangerous conduct" during the standoff.

Wong, during a visit to the headquarters of the Philippine Coast Guard, also announced a support package for the agency totaling 10 million Australian dollars ($6.7 million) for drone technology.

The US State Department also issued a statement criticizing China's actions, saying its "troubling pattern of provocations against the Philippines' legitimate maritime operations undermines regional peace and stability."

body.zh: 中国和菲律宾海军人员在有争议的南海发生暴力冲突后相互指责。这一事件加剧了马尼拉重大外交峰会前的紧张局势。 中国和菲律宾海军的水手在有争议的南海发生了桨和警棍对峙，菲律宾官员称，一名水手在争执中头部受伤。 最近的一次对抗发生在周一仁爱礁附近，这是两国此前曾多次发生冲突的争议地区。 菲律宾通过搁浅的 BRP Sierra Madre 军舰在该地区保持军事存在。 马尼拉表示，当菲律宾水手接近前哨基地时，中国海岸警卫队人员袭击了他们。 中国很快否认了这种说法。北京外交部在一份声明中表示，“菲律宾方面首先挑起事件”，乘坐小橡皮艇接近中国船只，但随后又“转而反指责，歪曲事实，恶意炒作”。 周二，中国召见菲律宾驻北京大使提出申诉，菲律宾也迅速与中国驻马尼拉大使进行跟进。 仁爱礁是南海有争议群岛南沙群岛的一部分。 南沙群岛是北京宣称对整个南海拥有主权的关键，南海是一条重要的全球贸易路线。 尽管海牙常设仲裁法院 2016 年裁定北京的主张没有法律依据，但北京仍然坚持对这条水道的主权主张。 中国一再要求拆除BRP马德雷山脉上的前哨基地，并用其船只包围了该环礁，造成了持续多年的紧张领土对峙。 这起事件发生在东南亚国家联盟 (ASEAN) 会议召开之前，该会议定于周二开始，十一个成员国和外部伙伴的外交部长参加了该会议。 正在马尼拉参加峰会的澳大利亚外交部长黄英贤周二谴责北京在对峙期间的“破坏稳定和危险的行为”。 黄在访问菲律宾海岸警卫队总部期间还宣布了为该机构提供总计 1000 万澳元（670 万美元）的无人机技术支持计划。 美国国务院也发表声明批评中国的行为，称其“对菲律宾合法海上行动的令人不安的挑衅模式破坏了地区和平与稳定”。 “我们与我们的盟友菲律宾站在一起，并赞扬......

reflection.en: This story draws attention to leadership, wisdom, and public responsibility. Proverbs 11:14 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with wisdom, integrity, and service, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到领导、智慧与公共责任。Proverbs 11:14提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以智慧、正直与服事来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: Chinese, Philippine personnel clash in the South China Sea
title.zh: 中菲人员在南海发生冲突

summary.en: Chinese Coast Guard and Philippine Navy personnel clashed in the South China Sea, resulting in a Philippine sailor sustaining a serious head injury. The incident involved the use of wooden batons during a confrontation between their boats.
summary.zh: 中国海警人员与菲律宾海军人员在南海发生冲突，双方船只上的队员使用木棍对峙，导致一名菲律宾水兵头部受重伤。

body.en: China Coast Guard personnel on a rigid hull inflatable boat clashed with Philippine Navy personnel aboard a rubber boat using wooden batons in the South China Sea on 20 July. According to Philippine authorities, one of their sailors suffered a serious head injury when a Chinese crew member allegedly struck him with a wooden baton.
body.zh: 7月20日，中国海警人员乘坐刚性充气艇与菲律宾海军人员乘坐橡皮艇在南海使用木棍发生冲突。据菲律宾当局称，一名中国船员据称用木棍殴打一名水手，导致其头部严重受伤。

reflection.en: The physical clash between personnel in the South China Sea highlights the fragility of peace in contested regions. Yahweh's word calls us to pursue peace actively, as far as it depends on us, even amidst disagreements. This incident reminds us of the constant need for restraint and diplomatic efforts to prevent escalation and injury.
reflection.zh: 南海人员之间的肢体冲突凸显了争议地区和平的脆弱性。雅伟的话语呼吁我们，只要力所能及，就要积极追求和平，即使在分歧之中也是如此。这一事件提醒我们，需要时刻保持克制并进行外交努力，以防止冲突升级和人员受伤。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: Chinese warship holds live-fire drills inside Japan’s economic waters for first time
title.zh: 中国军舰首次在日本专属经济区内举行实弹演习

summary.en: A Chinese missile destroyer conducted live-fire drills for the first time within Japan's exclusive economic zone, approximately 180km from Okinotori, Japan's southernmost island. This incident follows recent clashes between Chinese and Philippine sailors in the South China Sea, marking a significant escalation of...
summary.zh: 一艘中国导弹驱逐舰首次在日本专属经济区内举行实弹演习，地点距离日本最南端的冲之鸟岛约180公里。此次事件发生在中国和菲律宾水兵在南海发生冲突之后，标志着该地区军事活动的显著升级。

body.en: Exercise took place about 180km from Okinotori, Japan’s southernmost island, and comes as Chinese and Philippine sailors clashed in the South China Sea A Chinese missile destroyer fired live rounds for the first time inside Japan’s exclusive economic zone (EEZ) during a drill on Sunday, a day before Chinese and Philippine sailors clashed in the South China Sea. Three Chinese warships and a Russian frigate were spotted sailing between Okinawa’s main island and Miyako island into the Pacific on Thursday, before being picked up again around 330km south-west of Okinotori in the early hours of Sunday morning. Continue reading...
body.zh: 演习在距日本最南端岛屿冲之鸟岛约 180 公里处举行，正值中国和菲律宾船员在南海发生冲突。周日的演习中，一艘中国导弹驱逐舰首次在日本专属经济区 (EEZ) 内发射实弹，而前一天，中国和菲律宾船员在南海发生冲突。周四，三艘中国军舰和一艘俄罗斯护卫舰被发现在冲绳本岛和宫古岛之间驶入太平洋，周日凌晨在冲绳县西南约 330 公里处再次被发现。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The news of live-fire drills in contested waters can stir apprehension and fear about regional stability. In moments of geopolitical tension, Yahweh reminds us not to fear, for He is with us, strengthening and upholding us. His presence offers a steadfast anchor when nations assert power and threats loom.
reflection.zh: 在争议水域进行实弹演习的消息，可能引发人们对地区稳定的担忧和恐惧。在地缘政治紧张的时刻，雅伟提醒我们不要惧怕，因为他与我们同在，加固并扶持我们。当国家展示武力、威胁迫近时，他的同在提供了一个坚定的锚。

verse.textEn: So do not fear, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God.
verse.textZh: 你不要害怕，因为我与你同在；不要惊惶，因为我是你的神。

title.en: AliExpress fined record €550m by EU for failing to stop sale of illegal and fake goods
title.zh: 全球速卖通因未能阻止非法和假冒商品销售被欧盟罚款5.5亿欧元

summary.en: The Chinese online retail platform AliExpress has been fined €550 million by the EU for failing to prevent the sale of illegal and counterfeit products, including unsafe toys, on its platform.
summary.zh: 中国在线零售平台全球速卖通（AliExpress）因未能阻止其平台上销售非法和假冒产品（包括不安全玩具）而被欧盟处以5.5亿欧元的罚款。

body.en: Chinese retail platform handed penalty over listings for items such as counterfeit products and unsafe toys Business live – latest updates The Chinese online retail platform AliExpress has been fined a record €550m (£470m) by the EU over its failure to stop illegal goods including harmful clothing, cosmetics and kitchen gadgets being sold through its site. The European Commission fine is the biggest imposed by the bloc under Digital Services Act (DSA) legislation to protect consumers from illegal goods and deceptive or addictive marketing techniques. Continue reading...
body.zh: 中国零售平台对假冒产品和不安全玩具等商品进行处罚 Business live – 最新更新 中国在线零售平台速卖通因未能阻止通过其网站销售有害服装、化妆品和厨房用具等非法商品而被欧盟处以创纪录的 5.5 亿欧元（4.7 亿英镑）罚款。欧盟委员会的罚款是欧盟根据数字服务法 (DSA) 立法征收的最大一笔罚款，旨在保护消费者免受非法商品和欺骗性或成瘾性营销技术的侵害。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This significant fine highlights the critical importance of integrity in commerce and the responsibility of platforms to ensure fair and honest trade. Yahweh's word reminds us that dishonest practices, like false balances, are an abomination, while just weights bring delight. Upholding ethical standards protects consumers and builds trust in the marketplace.
reflection.zh: 这笔巨额罚款凸显了商业诚信的关键重要性，以及平台确保公平诚实贸易的责任。雅伟的话语提醒我们，不诚实的做法，如假秤，是祂所憎恶的，而公道的砝码则令祂喜悦。坚持道德标准能保护消费者，并在市场中建立信任。

verse.textEn: Yahweh detests dishonest scales, but accurate weights find favor with him.
verse.textZh: 诡诈的天平为雅伟所憎恶；公平的法码为他所喜悦。

title.en: The Guardian view on perceptions of superpowers: the world isn’t Chinamaxxing, it’s America-avoidant | Editorial
title.zh: 《卫报》观点：对超级大国的看法——世界并非在“中国化”，而是在“避开美国” | 社论

summary.en: Startling new research shows that in many countries – including old US allies – the public prefers Beijing to Washington. Earlier this year, a spate of Western TikTok and Instagram creators announced that they were at “a very Chinese time in my life” – drinking hot water and...
summary.zh: 一项令人震惊的新研究显示，在许多国家——包括美国的传统盟友——公众更倾向于北京而非华盛顿。今年早些时候，一些西方TikTok和Instagram创作者宣布他们正处于“我生命中非常中国化的时期”——喝热水并...

body.en: Startling new research shows that in many countries – including old US allies – the public prefers Beijing to Washington Earlier this year, a spate of western TikTok and Instagram creators announced that they were at “a very Chinese time in my life” – drinking hot water and wearing slippers around their homes. The Chinamaxxing phenomenon primarily reflected the constant need of influencers for novel content. But social media trends also reflect a growing fascination with China, as the economic historian Adam Tooze has noted . While it broods over China’s economic, military and technical advance, the Trump administration is accelerating Beijing’s diplomatic progress, as striking new polling by the Pew Research Center shows. For the first time, China and Xi Jinping are seen more favourably than the US and its president in most of the 36 major countries surveyed – including Canada, Mexico and Australia. Only in six countries did people rate the US more highly. While Beijing has seen significant improvements in some places, the slump in Washington’s standing is more dramatic. Across 20 countries, the median percentage with a favourable view of China rose from 32% to 46% between 2023 and this year; for the US, it fell from 58% to 36%. Views of China were much more positive in Latin America, Africa and parts of south and south-east Asia than in wealthier European and east Asian countries. Continue reading...
body.zh: 令人震惊的新研究表明，在许多国家 — — 包括美国的老盟友 — — 公众更喜欢北京而不是华盛顿。 今年早些时候，一大批西方 TikTok 和 Instagram 创作者宣布，他们正处于“我一生中非常中国化的时期”——喝着热水，在家中穿着拖鞋。 Chinamaxshing现象主要反映了网红对新颖内容的持续需求。但正如经济历史学家亚当·图兹（Adam Tooze）指出的那样，社交媒体趋势也反映出人们对中国日益增长的迷恋。皮尤研究中心令人震惊的最新民意调查显示，在关注中国经济、军事和技术进步的同时，特朗普政府正在加速北京的外交进展。在接受调查的 36 个主要国家（包括加拿大、墨西哥和澳大利亚）中，大多数国家对中国和习近平的好感度首次高于美国及其总统。只有六个国家的人们对美国的评价更高。尽管北京在某些方面取得了显着进步，但华盛顿的地位下滑更为严重。 2023 年至今，20 个国家对中国持好感的中位数百分比从 32% 上升至 46%；美国则从 58% 下降至 36%。拉丁美洲、非洲以及南亚和东南亚部分地区对中国的看法比富裕的欧洲和东亚国家要积极得多。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The shifting global perceptions of superpowers, as highlighted in the news, remind us that a nation's true standing is often tied to its character and actions. Proverbs 14:34 suggests that righteousness elevates a people, while moral failings can bring disgrace. This perspective encourages us to consider how nations, like individuals, are ultimately judged...
reflection.zh: 新闻中强调的全球对超级大国看法的转变，提醒我们一个国家真正的地位往往与其品格和行为息息相关。箴言14:34指出，公义使邦国高举，罪恶是人民的羞辱。这一视角鼓励我们思考，国家如同个人，最终会因其正直和所体现的价值观而受到评判。

verse.textEn: Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin condemns any people.
verse.textZh: 公义使邦国高举；罪恶是人民的羞辱。

title.en: Trump is invoking foreign election interference to justify his own | Jamil Smith
title.zh: 特朗普援引外国选举干预来为自己辩护 | 贾米尔·史密斯

summary.en: An article discusses how the former president's claims of foreign election interference are used to justify his own actions, leading him to treat voters who opposed him as suspects rather than legitimate participants in the democratic process.
summary.zh: 一篇文章讨论了前总统如何援引外国选举干预来为自己的行为辩护，导致他将反对他的选民视为嫌疑犯，而非民主进程的合法参与者。

body.en: The president no longer treats the people who defeated him as voters. He treats them as suspects There is a version of this country in which Donald Trump tells Americans the truth he has been handed: that their elections are secure. Once, he apparently wanted to. The Atlantic reported after Thursday night’s address that a February 2020 election-security briefing pleased Trump so much he wanted to announce the news himself. The press conference never happened. The election did, and Trump lost it. Continue reading...
body.zh: 总统不再将击败他的人视为选民。他将他们视为嫌疑人。这个国家有一个版本，唐纳德·特朗普告诉美国人他所得到的真相：他们的选举是安全的。有一次，他显然想要这么做。 《大西洋月刊》在周四晚上的讲话后报道称，2020 年 2 月的选举安全简报令特朗普非常高兴，他想亲自宣布这一消息。新闻发布会从未发生过。选举确实发生了，但特朗普输了。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The news highlights how a leader's refusal to accept election results and subsequent treatment of citizens as "suspects" can undermine trust and civic harmony. Proverbs 29:2 reminds us that the character of those in authority profoundly impacts the well-being of the people. When leaders govern with integrity and truth, society flourishes; when they do not,...
reflection.zh: 这则新闻揭示了领导人拒绝接受选举结果并将公民视为“嫌疑犯”的行为，如何损害信任和公民和谐。箴言29:2提醒我们，掌权者的品格深刻影响着民众的福祉。当领导人以正直和真理治理时，社会繁荣；反之，民众则会感到痛苦。

verse.textEn: When the righteous thrive, the people rejoice; when the wicked rule, the people groan.
verse.textZh: 义人增多，民就喜乐；恶人掌权，民就叹息。

title.en: Trump, not Iran, is the world’s greatest danger. He’s a one-man weapon of mass destruction | Simon Tisdall
title.zh: 特朗普，而非伊朗，是世界上最大的危险。他是一个人的大规模杀伤性武器 | 西蒙·蒂斯代尔

summary.en: The article argues that the US president's actions have initiated a disastrous war and an economic quagmire, leading to a "limitless fiasco" as bombing resumes. It characterizes the president as "feckless and clueless," unable to navigate or exit the conflict he started.
summary.zh: 文章指出，随着轰炸再次开始，美国总统的行为已将美国拖入一场无止境的灾难和经济泥潭。文章形容这位总统“无能又糊涂”，无法摆脱他所发动的这场灾难性战争。

body.en: As the bombing starts again, it’s clear the president has dragged the US into a limitless fiasco – and the world into an economic quagmire Feckless and clueless, Donald Trump is lost in Iran, unable to find a way out of the disastrous war he started. Once again, the US military is pummelling the country and, increasingly, its civilian infrastructure. As before, this unlawful bludgeoning strengthens the resistance of a hardline regime that cares little for its people’s suffering. How often have Trump and Pete Hegseth, the Pentagon’s wildling lord of bones, hailed a bogus victory? The president claimed this week to be “winning big”. No one believes him. Even as it counts the vast human and economic cost of his Persian folly, a watching world scoffs at US impotence. Control of the strait of Hormuz, closed due to Trump’s belligerence, is now the White House’s limited, elusive objective. The grander US and Israeli war aims – eliminating Iran’s nuclear programme, degrading its regional militias, regime change – are less attainable than ever. It’s Trump’s craven leadership that renders US forces ineffective, not the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. If Iran really is the existential menace he claims, the logical course would be all-out conquest. When George W Bush decided Iraq posed unacceptable dangers, he invaded with 170,000 ground troops. It was a catastrophe. But at least Bush had balls. Simon Tisdall is a Guardian foreign affairs commentator Continue reading...
body.zh: 随着轰炸再次开始，很明显，总统已将美国拖入了无限的惨败 — — 并将世界拖入了经济泥潭。 无能又无能的唐纳德·特朗普在伊朗迷失了方向，无法找到摆脱他发起的灾难性战争的出路。美国军队再次对该国进行打击，并越来越多地打击其民用基础设施。和以前一样，这种非法的殴打加强了一个不关心人民苦难的强硬政权的抵抗。特朗普和五角大楼的野人骸骨领主皮特·赫格斯多少次欢呼一场虚假的胜利？总统本周声称“大获全胜”。没有人相信他。尽管他的波斯愚蠢行为造成了巨大的人力和经济成本，但全世界都在嘲笑美国的无能。控制因特朗普的好战而关闭的霍尔木兹海峡，现在已成为白宫有限且难以捉摸的目标。美国和以色列更宏伟的战争目标——消除伊朗核计划、削弱其地区民兵、政权更迭——比以往任何时候都更难以实现。导致美军效率低下的是特朗普胆怯的领导，而不是伊斯兰革命卫队。如果伊朗确实是他所声称的生存威胁，那么合乎逻辑的路线将是全面征服。当乔治·W·布什认定伊拉克构成了无法接受的危险时，他派遣了 17 万地面部队入侵。这是一场灾难。但至少布什有胆量。西蒙·蒂斯达尔是卫报外交事务评论员继续阅读...

reflection.en: This proverb reminds us of the profound and often devastating impact that leaders can have on their people and the world. When those in power act recklessly or without wisdom, the consequences can be like a destructive force, leaving nations in turmoil and people vulnerable. It underscores the heavy responsibility of leadership and the need for discernment...
reflection.zh: 这句箴言提醒我们，领袖对他们的人民和世界可能产生深刻而往往是毁灭性的影响。当掌权者鲁莽行事或缺乏智慧时，其后果可能像一股破坏性的力量，使国家陷入混乱，人民变得脆弱。它强调了领导的重任以及对执政者保持明辨的重要性。

verse.textEn: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.
verse.textZh: 暴虐的君王辖制贫民，好像吼叫的狮子、觅食的熊。

title.en: 'Shocking vulnerabilities': Trump makes sweeping claims China meddled in US elections
title.zh: “令人震惊的漏洞”：特朗普就中国干预美国大选发表全面声明

summary.en: The US president made broad election security claims, laying groundwork for the federal government to take action.
summary.zh: 美国总统就选举安全问题发表了广泛声明，为联邦政府采取行动奠定了基础。

body.en:
In a speech attacking US election integrity on Friday, US President Donald Trump released intelligence that he said showed major Chinese interference in US elections, reviving his false claims he won the 2020 election.

Trump's allegations about the "shocking vulnerabilities" in the American electoral system appeared to lay the groundwork for the Republican to dispute the results of November's crucial US midterm elections .

It underscored Trump's effort to make election security a central political issue ahead of November's midterm vote, when Republicans in Congress will face the prospect of losing control of both the House of Representatives and Senate — an outcome that would carry significant political consequences for Trump.

"We can never watch a stolen election again," Trump said in the primetime address, referencing his 2020 presidential election defeat by Democrat Joe Biden.

Trump said he was declassifying huge amounts of intelligence data that showed, among other things, that superpower rival China had illicitly acquired 220 million US voter files.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"Over a period of years, starting during the 2020 election cycle, the People's Republic of China carried out what is believed to be the largest compromise of election data in history," Trump said in the televised speech from the White House.

He asserted that members of the US intelligence community deliberately suppressed information about the extent of China's activities.

His allegations contradict an unclassified 2021 US intelligence community assessment that found no indications any foreign actor tried to alter or succeeded in altering "any technical aspect" of the 2020 presidential election vote.

The assessment was conducted under John Ratcliffe, then Trump's director of national intelligence and now his CIA director.

Trump also claimed there were more than 250,000 non-US citizens registered to vote in four states.

Trump has persistently claimed his 2020 election defeat was "rigged," although more than 60 lawsuits produced no ruling establishing fraud capable of changing the outcome, while recounts, audits and his own justice department found none.

After railing against election security in the 25-minute address, Trump pressed Republicans in Congress to pass his signature elections legislation, the SAVE America Act, which has been stalled for months.

It seeks to impose new voter identification and citizenship requirements, despite longstanding findings that voter fraud in US elections is rare.

Election security experts have said these measures would make it harder for millions of eligible voters to cast a ballot.

body.en:
Less than four per cent of the social homes promised by the Albanese government's signature social housing fund have been delivered, two years into a five-year target period.

As of May 2026, 1432 of the Housing Australia Future Fund's target of 40,000 new social and affordable homes had been delivered, the Australian National Audit Office found in a report released on Tuesday.

The $10 billion fund's forecast to hit its target by mid-2029 faced "considerable uncertainty" as of June, the auditor-general found.

It's another setback for the government's broader housing supply agenda, with the construction industry about a year behind on its target to deliver 1.2 million new homes in the five years to June 2029.

Meanwhile, the social housing waitlist has grown from 155,000 to 169,000 in the 10 years to June 2024.

While Treasury was largely effective in designing the fund, the department had failed to take clear responsibility for delivering the program and provided little transparency about how it was progressing, the audit found.

Although funding applications opened in January 2024, Treasury had not finalised delivery arrangements until May 2026.

"The delayed finalisation of most governance and oversight arrangements has limited the ability of Treasury to systematically monitor and manage program risks and performance over time," the auditor-general said.

"Once finalised, Treasury has not always implemented governance and oversight arrangements as intended, with sometimes out-of-date and inconsistent arrangements.

The fund works by giving money to providers to either build new homes or purchase newly constructed homes from developers.

Once built, homes are subsidised by the government to provide tenants below-market rates for 25 years, at a cost of about $393,000 per dwelling in today's money.

Of the 1432 homes delivered by the fund, 762 were new homes constructed by housing providers, and 670 were newly built by private developers and purchased by a housing provider before, during or immediately after development.

The audit made five recommendations to improve governance, risk management, performance review and transparency of the program.

Housing Minister Clare O'Neil welcomed the report findings and accepted all recommendations.

"Importantly, the report found Treasury's design of the Housing Australia Future Fund was largely effective and supported by largely sound policy advice," she said.

body.en:
It's been nearly 60 years since a mysterious spy base was opened in a sacred stretch of Australian outback. Even today, what happens inside Pine Gap remains a closely guarded secret.

There's been renewed focus on the joint United States-Australian intelligence facility this week after hundreds of protesters gathered there to protest its existence.

Located 18km south-west of Alice Springs, the top-secret base is often described as one of Australia’s most secure and secretive facilities.

Its most recognisable feature is the cluster of large white domes scattered across the site. The facility uses satellite equipment to collect intelligence and detect missile launches.

The three-day gathering over the weekend marked the 60th anniversary of the agreement between the US and Australia that paved the way for the construction of the facility on Arrernte Country.

In a statement to SBS News, the defence department said the government does not comment on intelligence matters or the operation of its joint facilities.

The facility has been a source of scrutiny and controversy since it was established by the US' Central Intelligence Agency in the late 1960s to gather intelligence on Soviet missile tests during the Cold War.

It's expanded in scale and capacity over the decades, and has drawn repeated protest action, including a major demonstration in 1987 that saw more than 1,000 protesters march up to its gates. Organisers said Monday's protest was the largest since then.

In 1983, hundreds of women camped outside Pine Gap as part of a two-week peace protest, arguing it made Australia a nuclear target and tied the country to the US military machine.

In Alice Springs, where Census data puts the population at around 26,000, it employs around 800 of the town's residents, ABC Backstory reported in 2024. According to that reporting, locals remain divided over the facility.

Some view it as vital to the local economy, while some still fear it makes Alice Springs a nuclear target.

The Australian Federal Police, in a recruitment page for protective service officers at Pine Gap, describes it as one of its "most unique and critical protection sites".

Anti-war and anti- AUKUS campaigners, as well as pro-Palestinian solidarity groups, participated in the gathering over the weekend, calling for greater scrutiny of the facility's role in the Hamas-Israel war.

Last year, United Nations investigators accused Israel of committing genocide in Gaza during the war, an accusation which Israel denies.

One Nation leader Pauline Hanson says she's "totally opposed" to the war in Ukraine, but did not say whether she still believes that Russian President Vladimir Putin is a "strong man".

The right-wing leader was in Perth on Tuesday addressing a business breakfast after returning from Europe, where she faced scrutiny after holidaying in an Italian resort town with mining magnate Gina Rinehart, attending a luxury fashion show and speaking on a podcast with controversial far-right activist Tommy Robinson.

SBS News asked Hanson at a press conference on the sidelines of the business event whether she stood by her comments in 2017 praising Putin as a leader who had gained the respect of his country.

During the 2017 ABC Insiders interview, Hanson described Putin as a "patriotic" leader who was "doing so well for his country".

Putin has since been issued an arrest warrant by the world court for the 'unlawful deportation' of Ukrainian children in 2023. The Kremlin has rejected the accusation.

title.en: 'Unpredictable': New warning for Australians travelling abroad
title.zh: “不可预测”：澳大利亚政府对海外旅行发出新警告

summary.en: The Australian government has issued a new warning for citizens traveling abroad, citing escalating global conflicts that could lead to flight disruptions and changes to travel plans.

body.en:
The government is urging Australians to reconsider travel to Oman, Jordan and Saudi Arabia amid re-escalating conflict in the Middle East .

The latest advice on the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade's Smartraveller website said the situation in the Middle East "remains unpredictable" and there is "risk of more attacks and escalation".

"Military conflict in the Middle East has also caused widespread fuel supply shortages, flight cancellations and other travel disruptions worldwide," it said.

"Your travel plans may be affected, even if your destination is not in the Middle East."

The warning noted that military strikes and reprisal attacks have been carried out in a number of locations across the Middle East in recent days, including those directed at targets in each of the three countries.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Oman, Jordan and Saudi Arabia have been upgraded to level three, which advises Australians to reconsider their need to travel and avoid non-essential travel there.

Level three, according to the site's warning system, indicates serious and potentially life-threatening risks that can make a location unsafe for tourism and unsuitable for most travellers.

"We now advise 'reconsider your need to travel' overall due to the unpredictable security situation," Smartraveller said.

The three nations join Bahrain, Israel, Kuwait, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates at level three.

Iran, Iraq, Lebanon, the Palestinian territories, Syria and Yemen remain at the highest alert level, which advises Australians not to travel there at all.

For Australians already in the Middle East who want to leave, the government continues to advise them to do so while commercial flights are available if it's safe to travel to an airport.

A fragile ceasefire between the US and Iran has deteriorated this month. The warring nations have been exchanging strikes for days , pushing global oil prices upwards again, shocking markets and triggering renewed fears of a prolonged conflict.

On Monday, Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis declared a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia, raising alarm of further disruption to global trade and potentially opening a new front in the broader regional conflict.

title.en: A dark chapter of Australia's past is resurfacing in immigration politics

summary.en: Australia's past "White Australia policy" has re-entered public discussion as new immigration debates prompt concerns about the resurgence of its underlying discriminatory ideas.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚过去的“白澳政策”再次进入公众讨论，新的移民辩论引发了人们对其中歧视性思想复苏的担忧。

body.en:
One Nation leader Pauline Hanson has sparked a new discussion about the resurgence of a 'White Australia' policy — a controversial series of laws that discriminated against non-European migrants.

Hanson, during an appearance on a podcast with the British far-right, anti-immigration activist and convicted criminal Tommy Robinson last week, suggested that scrapping the White Australia policy was the root cause of apparent migration issues in Australia.

"It started in 1973 with Gough Whitlam, so they opened up and got rid of the White Australia policy, then they started bringing in the different migrants," she said.

She's since insisted that she doesn't support the policy, but a new wave of anti-immigration sentiment has sparked questions about whether Australia risks reviving aspects of it.

White Australia wasn't a single policy, but a series of laws that limited non-British migration to Australia.

"It essentially believed that Australia needed to be a homogenous white culture," Benjamin T Jones, an Australian political history expert, told SBS News.

"It prioritised immigration, especially from white British settlers, who they believed would integrate best into an Australian society."

It began with the Immigration Restriction Act 1901, which included a dictation test of 50 words in any European language, which became the way certain people ended up being excluded from Australia.

"You were never intended to pass it. It's a test that was designed to be failed," Mark Cully, the author of a new book on Australia's immigration economic history, told SBS News.

Even after the test was removed, it remained difficult for those who weren't European or North American to obtain permits to Australia, Cully says, and they were effectively excluded from applying for permanent residence.

The end of the White Australia policy began under Harold Holt in the 1960s, and it was dismantled under the Whitlam government in 1975, when the Racial Discrimination Act was passed, making it illegal to "offend, insult, humiliate or intimidate" someone because of their race.

"It's kind of astonishing in some ways that that policy, which is so ingrained and normalised and seen by many Australians as uncontroversial for 60 odd years, was then unwound, roughly over a decade," Cully said.
